note: Newest first, one entry per x.y series. The first entry's version is the exact version Range Book reports (for example 1.7.7); for a small change, bump that number and add to its items. Start a new entry for a new x.y series. Older entries use just x.y.

releases.title: Lowers, uppers, built guns and barrels
items: Gear & Ranges → Guns has a Lowers & uppers section. A lower has its manufacturer, model and serial number (no caliber); an upper has its cartridge, barrel length, twist, sight height and scope.

Put a lower and an upper together to make a gun: on a gun's page choose Made as: A lower + an upper and pick them (or tap Make a gun with this lower or upper). The gun uses the upper's specs and the lower's serial number. One lower can be in several guns, so you set up each combination once and just pick the gun on Shooting, Reloading or a range day.

Barrels for complete guns: add them under Barrels or on the gun's page, with their own cartridge, length, twist, sight height and scope (blank boxes use the gun's). When you pick a gun that has barrels on a Shooting load, a Reloading recipe or Start a range day, Range Book asks which barrel you're using.

Lowers, uppers and barrels each keep their own round count (uppers and barrels also barrel life), and cleaning reminder. Range trips and ladders remember what they were shot with, so changing a gun later doesn't move old rounds. Worn or due-for-cleaning parts show on Home.
The guns Excel export and the full Excel export have a Lowers uppers barrels tab, and a Built from column for guns made of a lower and an upper.

Import from a spreadsheet has Lowers, Uppers and Barrels tabs, and Lower and Upper columns on the Guns tab, so you can bring in built guns and barrels too. Download the template again to get the new tabs.

In the Guns list, lowers that are already in a gun and barrels that are on a gun are shaded, so the free ones stand out. When you put a gun together, the Upper list starts each upper with its cartridge and is sorted by it.

releases.title: Gun types, manufacturer and model
items: A gun's Name is now two boxes, Manufacturer and Model (Manufacturer suggests common makers as you type). Everywhere a gun is listed or picked, it shows the two together, like Tikka T3x Lite. Guns you already had are split for you: a name that starts with a maker Range Book knows (Tikka, Ruger, Smith & Wesson and about 60 more) has it moved to Manufacturer, and any other name stays whole in Model.
Each gun has a Type: Rifle, Pistol or Shotgun (pistol includes revolvers). Pick it on the gun's page under its name.
The Guns list on Gear & Ranges is grouped by type: rifles, then pistols, then shotguns, then any gun without a type, each sorted by name.

When you fill in a gun's cartridge, Range Book guesses its type (a handgun cartridge means a pistol, a gauge means a shotgun) and says so; tap another type if it's wrong. Guns you already had get a guessed type the same way.
The import template's Guns tab has a Type column with a drop-down list. A blank Type is guessed from the cartridge, and words like handgun, revolver, carbine and shotgun are understood.
The guns export (Excel and PDF) and the full Excel export have a Type column and list guns by type.

The import template's Guns tab has Manufacturer and Model columns instead of Name. A spreadsheet with a single Name column still works: a known maker at the start is moved to Manufacturer. The guns exports have Manufacturer and Model columns.

releases.title: Import from a spreadsheet
items: Account → Import from a spreadsheet (also on the Gear & Ranges and Components lists) adds guns, scopes, factory ammo, bullets, powders, primers and brass from Excel, Numbers or Google Sheets (.xlsx or .csv).

Download the template: a tab for each kind of gear, an example row on each, drop-down lists for cartridges, BC type, focal plane, MIL/MOA and primer sizes, and tips on columns like Twist. Or download it with your gear already filled in, change things in the spreadsheet and import it back as updates.
Your own spreadsheets work too: columns are matched by their headings, and you're asked about any column it doesn't recognize (pick what it is, add it to Notes, or leave it out).

Cartridges, BC types, primer sizes and scopes it doesn't know are listed once each so you can pick the right one or keep what you typed. A scope it doesn't know can be added as a new one. Numbers and dates it can't read are shown so you can fix them. Units like 610 mm, 2,700 fps, $32.99 and 1:8 twist are understood.

Anything already in Range Book is shown side by side with what's different, and you choose Skip, Update it or Add as new (or the same for all). Rows that match exactly are left alone. Nothing is saved until you tap Import.
Import from a spreadsheet: the side-by-side table for things already in Range Book no longer shades every other row unevenly.

releases.title: Syncing between devices
items: Changes from your phone and computer are now combined when they sync, instead of the last device to save replacing everything. This includes changes made on a phone with no signal.

It works piece by piece: if one device changed a load's velocity and the other changed its name, you keep both. Guns, ammo, trips, loads and recipes added on either device are all kept, and a delete on one doesn't undo an edit made later on the other.
When both devices changed the very same thing, the newer edit wins, going by when you made it (a change made offline keeps the time you made it, not the time it synced).
This also fixes a computer left open for a while undoing changes made on another device when it saved.

releases.title: Cartridges
items: A list of about 115 rifle, handgun and rimfire cartridges with each one's true bullet diameter and the SAAMI (or C.I.P.) maximum case length and overall length. Type any name for one (3006, 308 Win, 7.62 NATO, 6.5 CM) on a gun, recipe, ammo or Shooting load and pick it; it fills in the bullet diameter.
Guns have a Cartridge (the one it's chambered for).

Warnings when ammo doesn't fit its gun: a banner on the Shooting load and a Check cartridge tag in the lists. Safe one-way pairs pass (38 Special in a 357 Magnum, 223 in a 5.56, 44 Special in a 44 Magnum and more); the reverse is flagged as dangerous, and so is 300 Blackout with a 5.56/.223 gun.
Recipes and ammo warn when the bullet's diameter doesn't match the cartridge, the case length is over the maximum, or the COAL is longer than the SAAMI maximum.
Cartridges you'd typed with another name for a listed one now use its standard name, so loads group together. The guns export has a Cartridge column.

Tools → Cartridges shows the whole list (for reference only). Change any number or name you find wrong: changed boxes are colored, with Revert to put the original back. Add your own cartridges (✕ deletes them). Your changes are used everywhere and sync to your other devices.
The Shooting tab's ammo picker tags subsonic ammo with Sub.
Dope card: smaller From, To and Every boxes with Reticle: elevation beside them, the Zeroed at line just above the card, and the card and reticle line up at the top.
Picking a gun whose scope has MOA or MIL turrets ticks the matching Adjust column in the range table (and the wind column follows). The range table has a bar under it to make it taller or shorter.
Wind starts at 0 on a new load.
The Point-blank range card no longer has Show it on the chart or Set my scope to this zero: the point-blank zero is always on the chart, and you pick it with the circle in its zero box.

When spin drift can't be worked out, a Spin drift is off note shows above the range table and the dope card saying what's missing (bullet length, twist or diameter), with a button that takes you to it.

Picking ammo on the Shooting tab fills in the bullet length from the ammo, or from its reloading recipe or its saved bullet under Components when the ammo doesn't have one. Refill from recipe on reloaded ammo now copies the bullet length too.
With the Cartridge filled in on a Shooting load, the ammo picker shows only ammo for that cartridge (and ammo that's safe in it). Show all cartridges at the top of the list shows everything.
Dope card: MOA / MIL is now one button that shows the unit and switches when you tap it, so it fits beside Reticle: elevation.

releases.title: Gear & Ranges
items: Guns & Ammo is now Gear & Ranges, with four sections: Guns, Ammo, Scopes and Ranges.

Saved ranges moved to Gear & Ranges → Ranges: each range has its own page to edit its targets, and a Dope section that shows the dial and wind for every target with any Shooting load. Your ranges carry over as they were.
Shooting loads keep a Saved ranges card that shows a range's dope for that load, with Edit ranges › to go change it.
Fixed: a scope's reticle picture could fail to show on the dope card on some devices. If it can't be used (its scale isn't set, or it hasn't loaded yet), the reticle now says why.

Fixed: setting a reticle picture's scale sometimes didn't save, when the app refreshed in the background while the picture uploaded or the scale window was open (switching apps or the photo picker on an iPad can do that).

Bullet path: the first zero box is now your point-blank zero (purple), worked out from the target size in the Point-blank range card, followed by three zeros you type. The chart shows four paths instead of five. If you had a fourth zero, it moved into an empty box (or replaced zero 3 if it was the one your scope was set to).
The Range table and Dope card say at the top which zero they're using.

Reloading recipes and ammo have a Supersonic / Subsonic button next to Cartridge. Subsonic ones are tagged in the Reloading, Ammo and Shooting lists (a Shooting load gets the tag from the ammo it uses).
Shooting load tiles list the point-blank zero first.

releases.title: A tour of each tab
items: Each tab (Home, Shooting, Reloading, Guns & Ammo and Tools) has a Tour button next to Help that walks through what that tab does, card by card. On a phone the two buttons are small icons at the top right.
The scope list has about 90 models now, with many more from Vortex, Sig Sauer and Primary Arms (hunting, long-range and 1-6x to 1-10x scopes).

Scopes can have turrets in other units than the reticle (a MIL reticle with MOA turrets): the dope card dials in the turret's units and the reticle holds stay in the reticle's. A click value can be left as not published.

releases.title: Scopes and your own reticle
items: Guns & Ammo → Scopes: add your scopes from a list of about 40 popular ones (power, focal plane, MOA or MIL, click value and reticle name from the makers' published specs), or enter one yourself, and put each on a gun.
A gun's scope sets MOA or MIL for every Shooting load that uses it, and its name goes on the dope card.
Second focal plane scopes: enter the power the marks are true at, then pick the power you're on under the dope card's reticle and the hold is worked out in marks.
Change how it looks: a window with a preview to set the plain reticle's marks, holdover dots, numbers, center and lines so it looks like yours.
Use a picture of your own reticle: upload it to the scope, tap the center and a mark a known distance away, and the dope card puts the dot on your reticle. Private to you and in your backups.
The guns Excel and PDF exports list each gun's scope.
Each new version shows a beta notice once, which has to be dismissed: Range Book is still in beta and not everything has been tested thoroughly.

releases.title: Help where you need it
items: Each page has a Help button at the top right that opens How to Use right at the part about what you're looking at, with a Back button to return.
Cards on Shooting loads, Reloading loads, guns, ammo, components and in Tools have a small ⓘ next to their title: tap it for a quick how-to, and More in How to Use for the full story.
Printable targets are listed from one aim point to the most, on each paper size (and in a range trip's Print a target list).
Fixed: after an update, Chrome over https could keep showing the old list of printable targets (and the old What's new).

The Dope card and Reticle holds are one card: one MOA / MIL switch sets both, and tapping a distance on the card shows it on the reticle (beside the card on an iPad or computer; on a phone it slides up, with ‹ › to step through the distances).

releases.title: Hit chance, reticle holds, saved ranges and more
items: Tools → Hit chance: your odds of a first-round hit at a distance from your group size, velocity SD and how sure you are of the wind and range, with a picture of the spread, what would help most, and the same target at other distances.
Shooting loads have Reticle holds: a plain MIL or MOA reticle with a dot where the target goes for any distance, holding everything or dialing elevation and holding wind.
Saved ranges: save the places you shoot with each target's distance, angle and size, and see the dial and wind for every target with any load. Range names show up under Where on range trips.
Range trips record the cold-bore shot, and each gun's page has a Cold-bore log that shows where your first shot tends to land.

Ladder groups have Pressure signs (flat or cratered primers, ejector marks, heavy bolt lift, sticky extraction, loose primer pockets, case head expansion), marked on the velocity chart, in the Summary and in the exports.
Live target remembers the order of the holes, so a group shows Shot by shot: each shot's velocity next to where it hit, and whether faster shots hit higher.
Live target works on any target: tap its four corners, give its size and tap the aim points.
Take the tour is now at the top of How to Use, so it's easy to find on an iPad or computer (on a phone it's also under More).

Bigger printable targets from a home printer: two Letter pages taped together into an 11 × 16 inch target, with 1, 2, 4 or 8 aim points. Measuring a photo and Live target recognize them by themselves.
Fixed: a photo of the Letter 1 big aim point target could be read as the 11 × 17 one, which made its groups measure too big.

releases.title: A quick tour
items: New accounts get a short tour the first time they sign in: Home, Shooting, Reloading, Guns & Ammo, Tools, How to Use (and Admin, for admins). It only points things out and changes nothing. Skip it any time.
Take it again whenever you like: More → Take the tour on a phone, or How to Use → Getting started → Take the tour.

releases.title: Control Live target from your iPad
items: Tap Remote on the phone's Live target screen, then Tools → Live target → Watch on your iPad (or any device signed in to your account). The iPad shows the phone's screen and group numbers and can tap Shot, Undo, Next aim, Whole target and Save, set the charge, shots and distance, pick the microphone sensitivity, and add or remove marks by tapping the picture, so you never touch the phone on the scope.
It works through your Range Book server, so both devices need a signal (an iPad on the iPhone's hotspot works). Nothing from it is saved; it stops when you tap Remote again or close Live target.
Red Night now turns the Live target camera picture fully red.
The README on GitHub has a new "No server? Here's how" section with ways to run Range Book without a home server.

releases.title: Live target
items: New Live target: put your phone on a spotting scope, aim it at a printed Range Book target, and Range Book marks each shot as it lands. Tap Shot after each shot, or turn on Listen for shots to have the microphone hear them (only when nobody is shooting near you).

Listen for shots has a Sensitivity setting: Normal, Suppressed, and Quiet .22 for a suppressed .22 or subsonic loads. A white mark on the sound bar shows how loud a shot has to be, so you can see whether yours reach it.

It zooms in on the aim point you're shooting at but keeps watching the whole page, and widens the view by itself when a shot lands outside the zoom. Group size, MOA, mean radius and the group's center from the aim point update after every shot.

Tap a hole to add one it missed, or a mark to remove it. Save makes one measured photo of the target, and each charge gets its group size, mean radius and distance. Open it from a ladder (next to + Photo) or a range trip.

Live target is also in Tools, so you can use it without a load or a range trip. Save keeps the target photo and its measured groups in your Range Book (it waits on the phone if there's no signal), listed under Tools → Live target → Saved. Later, move one into a range trip (or use + Saved Live target in the trip) or into a reloading ladder. Share picture gives you a picture of the target with each group and its numbers.

releases.title: Mean radius, backups and import
items: Measuring a target photo now keeps the group's mean radius (the average distance of every hole from the group's center) and where the group's center landed from the aim point. Both show on each group, and Mean radius gets its own column in the Summary, Combine matching charges, and the Excel and PDF exports. Groups you measured before fill in by themselves when you open the load.
Account → Download backup saves everything in your account in one .zip file, photos included.

Account → Import brings in a backup or an Excel export (from now on, Excel files carry a hidden copy of your data). It adds to your account and skips anything already there, so nothing is deleted or doubled. Use it to restore, or to move to another Range Book.
Admins can download any person's backup from the Admin page.

releases.title: Tools
items: New Tools area: a tab on a computer, More → Tools on a phone, and the Tools button on Home. It opens to a tile for each tool (Twist & stability, MOA · MIL · inches, Powder per container, Convert and Printable targets) with a line about what it does; tap one to open it and ‹ Tools to go back. Nothing in Tools is saved.

Twist & stability tells you whether a bullet is stable in your barrel's twist (the Miller formula, corrected for velocity, temperature and altitude) and the slowest twist that fully stabilizes it. Pick a Bullet from your Components and a Gun side by side, or type the numbers in.

MOA/MIL turns a group or hold into MOA and MIL at any distance (or back). Powder works out rounds per container, powder cost per round and how much powder a batch needs. Convert does grains/grams, fps/m·s, inches/mm, yards/metres and foot-pounds/joules.
Printable targets moved into Tools (Tools → Targets).

On a Shooting load, Check barrel twist (under Inputs) opens Twist & stability filled in from that load. A warning also appears at the top of a load when its bullet isn't fully stable in that twist under today's conditions.
Fixed: if you changed a number box and then typed the original number back, Range Book kept the in-between value. It now goes back to exactly what was saved.

releases.title: Range Book 2.0
items: Range Book 2.0 is the first release for everyone: free software you can install on your own server from https://github.com/saoneill01-a11y/rangebook.

A new account's Shooting list starts with just the SAMPLE · 6.5 Creedmoor load. The other built-in example loads (.22 LR, .308, 300 Blackout, 6mm ARC and the rest) are gone. Accounts that already have them keep them and can delete them like any other load.

releases.title: Metric units, combined charges, pull to refresh
items: More → Account → Units switches between Imperial and Metric. Metric shows metres, m/s, centimetres (millimetres for cartridge sizes), joules, °C, km/h, metres of altitude and kilograms of powder. Bullet weights and powder charges stay in grains. It covers the whole app, the Excel and PDF exports and printed targets. Your data doesn't change, only how it's shown, and the setting follows your account to your other devices.

Pull to refresh in the home-screen app: at the top of any page, pull down until it says Release to refresh and let go. It saves anything you were typing, then reloads with the newest data, so a change made on your computer shows up on your phone without closing the app.

With two or more ladders, the Summary and charts have a Combine matching charges button. Each charge is shown once with every shot at that charge from all your ladders pooled: combined average velocity, SD, ES and the average group. Your ladders and their shots aren't changed.
Tap a ladder's title (Ladder 1, Ladder 2…) to fold it down to its title and summary line. Each phone or computer remembers which ladders you folded.

Distance moved to the top of each ladder, next to the Loaded date, Tested date and Temperature. Enter it once and every group in that ladder uses it for its MOA; each ladder can have its own distance. Existing ladders took the distance most of their groups used, and the folded ladder's summary line shows it.
On Shooting and Reloading, an open load's name sits in large type at the right end of the bar of links, so it stays in view as you scroll. The big page title is hidden while a load is open.
Importing a chronograph spreadsheet (RangeCraft or Garmin .xlsx) works again on the home-screen app, and works without a signal after the first import.

The new-version banner (Reload now) and the "Range Book was updated" note float at the bottom of the screen, just above the tabs on a phone, so you see them wherever you are on the page. The app now checks for a new version when it opens, when your phone gets its signal back and every minute while it's open, and tries again shortly if the server was restarting, so the Reload now prompt shows up within about a minute of an update.

On Shooting, every load can now be deleted, including the example loads Range Book starts with (.22 LR, .308, 6mm ARC and the rest). Open the load and tap Delete load at the very bottom; Undo brings it back. The examples also keep a separate Reset to defaults button.
The "Group (MOA)" label on the Velocity by charge chart is no longer cut off.
What's new is shorter: one entry for each version series instead of one for every small update.

Range Book is now free software under the GNU AGPL-3.0, copyright Sean O'Neill: anyone can use, change and share it, and anyone who shares or hosts a changed version has to share their code too. See How to Use → License.

New installs start with a made-up SAMPLE · 6.5 Creedmoor load: a worked-up ladder on Reloading (first account) and a matching load on Shooting. Both carry a warning that the numbers are examples, not load data, and must be checked against a load manual. The real reloading data that used to ship for a new install has been removed from the code; existing installs keep all their data.
Range Book is published on GitHub. How to Use → License links to its source code, and a few messages that were written just for the original install now read for everyone.

releases.title: Pick the range table columns
items: Under the range table, tick Adjust (MOA), Adjust (MIL) and Wind to choose which of those columns to show. Wind includes the wind brackets and spin drift. Range, velocity, energy, time and the path are always there.
It starts with just Adjust (MOA), so the table is much narrower. Your choice is remembered on each phone or computer.

releases.title: Ladder tests
items: Groups is now called Ladder tests, and a load can hold several ladders, each with its own groups. The Loaded date, Tested date and Temperature are at the top of each ladder. Plan a new ladder or + Empty ladder starts another one without touching the first.
Target photos belong to the ladder you shot them with. Each ladder has its own + Photo button, and Shot with in the photo moves it to another ladder.
With more than one ladder, the Summary and charts show one ladder at a time; pick another or All ladders from Showing.
Each ladder has a Take components out of inventory button that takes its bullets, primers and powder out of Components and counts a loading on the brass lot. Put them back undoes it.

Shot boxes are sized for a 4-digit speed, five to a row. + Shot adds one; − Shot lets you pick one or more shots and delete them, with Undo. Range trips work the same way, and + Type in shots starts a string you type in yourself.
Every group uses the bullet weight from the recipe. Group size sits right next to Distance.
The range table shows one Path column, for the zero you picked.
Sign in at home at http://<server IP>:9090 as well as through your Cloudflare address. Offline use, Use the weather where I am and Field mode's keep-awake need the https address.
The app is sent compressed, about a quarter of its old size, so it opens faster on a weak signal.
What's new on How to Use stays folded until you tap it.
The Excel export has a Ladder Tests sheet with a Ladder column (also on Photos and Loads).

releases.title: Angle, wind, temperature, compare and labels
items: Shot angle: on the Conditions card, enter how steeply you're shooting up or down hill. The table, chart and dope card show the smaller hold you need.

Wind direction: enter the wind's speed and the o'clock it comes from, and the calculator works out the push and which way to hold. A switch adds 5, 10 and 15 mph wind brackets to the range table, dope card and Field mode.

Powder temperature sensitivity: enter the temperature your velocity was measured at and how many fps it changes per 10°F, and muzzle velocity adjusts for today. A chart under a load's Range trips plots velocity against temperature, and one tap uses its trend.
Compare loads: on the Reloading list, pick up to three loads to see them side by side, with the best numbers highlighted.
Labels: ammo box labels for each logged batch, and a ladder test label with every charge numbered and a box to tick as you load it, plus Loaded and Tested dates.
Groups have Loaded and Tested dates and a Temperature, also in the Excel export.

releases.title: Chart, zeros, ammo and update banner
items: Bullet path chart: drag the bar under it to make it taller or shorter (it keeps its shape), Declutter hides the yardage labels, and True scale draws the flight at its real proportions. It starts at half its old height.
Each zero has one box under the chart with its near, far and top numbers. Pick the circle in a box for the zero your scope is set to; the range table and dope card use it.
Weather has its own Conditions card under Inputs.
On a Shooting load, sight height and twist come from the picked gun, and bullet length, weight, BC and diameter from the picked ammo. + Enter new factory ammo opens Guns & Ammo to add one.
Reloaded ammo has a Locked switch and Duplicate, and picks its bullet, powder, primer and brass from Components.
Add a powder from the list has a search box.
Reloading has a Load view (a read-only load sheet for the bench) and a Notes page for notes that aren't about one load.
When the server has a new version, a banner offers Reload now, even if the app has been open the whole time.
Swiping in from the left edge to go back is quicker on iPhone, and the boxes you tap to open a load, gun or ammo stand out more.

releases.title: Simpler reloading
items: Each load has two views: Develop (recipe, groups, ladder, charts, targets) and Load (the finished load and your loaded rounds).
Working charge: tap This is my load next to a charge in the Summary. It's used when you log batches, add the load to your ammo, work out the cost or use it in the calculator.
Locked switch: a finished load can be locked so its recipe, groups and working charge can't be changed.
Recipe parts picked from Components fold to one line with a Change link and a Done button.
Logging a batch adds the rounds to your ammo inventory by itself.
+ New load asks for the cartridge, gun and parts from Components, then can go straight to the ladder planner. Duplicate can swap in a different powder or bullet.

releases.title: Reloaded ammo and Components
items: Reloaded ammo inventory: add a recipe's ammo from Loaded rounds, or make an entry by hand under Guns & Ammo → Ammunition. Batches you log add to the count, and range trips count it down. Entries can pick their parts from Components for a cost per round.
The Ammunition box on a Shooting load is a short, searchable list of your reloaded ammo, your factory ammo and the catalog.

Components: a list of about 150 popular powders, brass lots with a case length, and Update buttons that copy changed component details into the loads that use them. A Components › button on a load jumps there and back.
A recipe's Case is now called Brass and can be picked from your brass lots.
Guns & Ammo → Guns has Export Excel and Export PDF for just your guns, with a photo page per gun.
Each section of How to Use folds up, and every card in Guns & Ammo → Ammunition folds too.

releases.title: First numbered release
items: Version number and this What's new page.
Cost per round from what you paid for bullets, powder, primers and brass.
LabRadar import into Reloading groups and range trips.
A welcome page where the first person on a new install creates the admin account.
Nosler and Barnes factory ammo in the catalog (about 155 loads), and picking factory ammo straight from the catalog on Shooting.
A Range trips page with every trip in one list, gun photos and serial numbers, swipe back from the left edge, and collapsible cards.
